# Chapter Four: A Hunting We Will Go

The two began a search pattern starting where the original group of police and search dogs had looked and started working their way through the wooded area around the path of the canal “So Sam why does it feel like we are being put to busy work to keep us out of the way” he asked his friend while they walked Sam shook his head “Probably because we are” he said frankly.

As the Bishop approached the crime scene Edgar intercepted him. “Sir, he touched the cross” Talbot gave him an annoyed look “and” Edgar looked around to ensure he wouldn’t be overheard, “It felt hot” Talbot nodded “I thought as much, call in Miller and Schultz I want them close” Edgar looked at the older man “You are using him as bait aren’t you” he accused. Talbot shot the larger man a sharp look “Watch yourself, remember who you work for, and yes I am, we need to know what’s going on and if we have a chance to bring them to us, we will use it, understood” he said harshly. Edgar looked down, “Yes sir” and he walked away pulling out his cell phone.

Edgar had been a hunter going on 20 years now and there were still some aspects of the job he didn’t like. He knew the pack was watching from somewhere close, he could sense it, but for what, why all the searching and the specific kills al over the united states. None of this bode well for the situation and now the Bishop was using this poor sap as bait, god help him and his family should they take notice of him. The phone rang once and a woman with a heavy German accent answered “What” Edgar smiled, Shultz was a good hunter and came off like a hard ass, but the woman was all heart underneath. “Shultzy its Bear” using there nicknames for each other “Need you in DC as of yesterday, can you get away” It took a moment and then a heavy sigh came across the line “I am going to lose my tail on this one, is it that important?” she asked annoyed. “The old man thinks it is” Another silence “I’ll be there tomorrow” she said and hung up. He made the second call to Miller who also said he would be there tomorrow as well. With that done he went about his own duties, He wanted to know what they were up against.

He walked over to one of the Park Police who was monitoring the crime scene, a bulky man of about 50 from the looks of him. “Officer, do you have a boat available”

It took 20 minutes for one to arrive but once it was there Edgar relieved the pilot much to the man’s protests and took the boat across the falls to the other bank. He tied down the boat and stepped onto the shore, His right hand was in his jacket wrapped around a 45 caliber pistol with silver hollow point ammo, he didn’t think they would be stupid enough to attack in daylight, but then again he didn’t think they would leave calling cards like the one across the falls.

With his left hand he held the cross and began to pass it over the bank as it got warmer he moved in that direction until he came across boot prints in the mud. Careful not to step onto them Edgar walked around the area. Three of them, two males and a female, he thought, all wearing cowboy or more likely biker boots. They were here as humans so it was likely they were waiting to see who showed up for this little event. This did not bode well for anyone on the scene of this crime. Edgar followed the foot prints beyond the bank until he couldn’t see them anymore. Once they disappeared into the underbrush, the cross came back up. It worked similar to a homing beacon, it would tell the direction of a creature who was cursed with the affliction, it was something that allowed hunters an easy way to help hunt the creatures down. He closed his eyes and said something in Aramaic, when he opened his eyes, they were white and he could see head signatures in the trees. Allowing him to tell what was ahead and waiting for him, If anything.

His other hand never left the pearl handled 45, if they were still around he didn’t want any surprises. He had been wrong, only three had attended the coast but it seemed another three had been back further in the woods two more females and a male. He was sure if he followed further he would find a back road and Bike tracks. They were gone. H went back to the shore to get on the board when he found a small sim card, the kind you used in camera’s. He picked it up and looked it over, it seemed to be intact, this probably meant that they were not only staking out but takin pictures. He pocketed the drive and made his way back to the boat, whomever had been here were long gone now.

Sam and Vic continued to search the woods for close to two hours before giving up and going back to the crime scene, the police and forensics were cleaning up and looked to be packing up shop for the most part. They would leave techs here to comb over the short but the consensus was because of the location and the water, they wouldn’t find enough that would give them any solid leads.

Bishop Talbot was talking to the guys from Justice and Edgar seemed to have taken off. “Let me see if we have a next move, give me a second” Sam walked over to the bishop and they talked for a bit. Afterwards he returned and shrugged “They are going to close the park for a bit, however you are still tasked to us, we have some things to take care of but you will be on call, so feel free to head home my friend, if we need you we will call” he said with a smile, Vic could tell there was more to it, but didn’t want to push. “Alright, you have my cell if you need me” And he headed back towards the visitor’s center on foot.

He made his way down the path, and leaned his head back to enjoy the sun, it had been a hell of a morning he kept going back to the body, who had it been, what were they doing and more importantly, who would do that to someone. From what he had been able to infer from the different conversations it had been left more like a trophy or a calling card, but for what and for whom he didn’t know. As he walked he started to get the oddest feeling

It was like he was being watched, he looked around checking the Woodline and didn’t see anything but still couldn’t seem to shake the thought. There was a snap of a twig somewhere off to his left and he thought he heard someone snicker. Damn kids he thought, sneaking in to get a look at what was going on. Vic should his head and stepped over to the wood line alright if the kids wasn’t to play grab ass at a crime scene he would give them a little bit of a scare “Come out of there and show yourself, this is the Park Police, you are in a restricted area” Vic said in his best official voice. He scanned the Woodline looking for any movement and saw none, in fact the woods were still, no birds or insects, just dead quiet, now that was odd he thought to himself.

Just odd, he had spent enough time hunting with his grandfather as a kid to know that something was off, whatever it was had the entire woods freaked out enough to go into hiding. He took a step into the Woodline still scanning from left to right, to try and catch a glimpse of whatever it was. There was movement, it was a bit distant, a dog or something maybe yellow eyes he squinted and tried to get a better look. It moved forward slightly hunching down. It was too big to be a dog but…

At that moment Sam laid a hand on his shoulder and Vic just about jumped out of his skin “Hey you okay” he asked. Vic turned back to the woods, but whatever had been there was gone now. “Yeah, just thought.” and looked at Sam, he must have looked a bit spooked because Sam’s face looked concerned “What is it”. Vic took one more look at the Woodline and then shook his head. “Nothing, don’t worry about it, you coming back to the visitor’s center with me” He clapped his friend on the shoulder “Yeah I’ve got to get back to report in” he said and they walked towards the center.

Marcus

Within the Woodline covered in shadow Marcus waited, he could see the two, smell them as they passed. The one in uniform smelled familiar like a scent he knew but couldn’t place. The priest he knew well; they had been tracking his kind for ages. He could smell one of the order as a matter of course. It was part of their training, identify and mark the threat that way you knew when it was near. But the other, was something else, he knew the man from the order, but was not part of that pack. His human mind still in control even in this form. The animal mind, the one he held back cataloged everything, every smell and sound waiting to be let out to hunt. As time went on it took less and less effort to stave off the animal, he knew there were some who welcomed it and even some more who changed and never went back becoming the animal. He did not know why and did not care to. He only knew this was his packs way and it worked for him, allowing him the ability and the power without the need to give into the hunter and the predator that was in him.

Now was not the time and Marcus knowing it, aside from the police, the order was here and they were not to be trifled with lightly, they had what they wanted, they had left the body of the Child Killer where it would be found. The piece of shit had been killing kids up and east coast for a year now though the authorities didn’t know it, the pack had tracked him and when they found him they exacted revenge for those children. But they used the body to draw out the order, and something else, they were told it had to be here, that they would know why soon. their Alpha was insistent, so they had obeyed.

Had he found what they were looking for in this man, the smell marked him as something almost familiar. He turned and headed back to where the rest of the members waited. He would report what he had found and they would watch until they were told to do otherwise.

He padded back to the others and changed, once he was dressed he approached the bikes as they set on the road outside of the park. “I am not sure but I think I might have found what we were looking for, we need to report back” he explained the smell and the look of the person who he had tracked it from “Rebecca, I need you to see if you can keep an eye on him, for now until we know what our orders are” The tall raven haired female nodded her forest green eyes never leaving his. She mounted her matte black custom sportster and sped off towards the park entrance.

The others situated themselves and headed back towards Rockville to report to the alpha, this was to be done in person, never over the phone. Per his request. They had a safe house in the historic district in downtown Rockville that they were using as a base during this operation.
